title: 2020 roadmap on pore materials for energy and environmental applications
claim: MOF pores and binding sites can reduce polysulfide migration in lithium–sulfur batteries through selective transport and chemical trapping.
explanation: The review discusses sulfur confinement, Lewis-acidic Ni sites that bind polysulfides, and a microporous HKUST-1@GO separator that passes lithium ions while blocking polysulfide intermediates.
scope: MOF-containing cathodes and separators in lithium–sulfur batteries.
conditions: Pore accessibility and the chemical affinity of framework sites for polysulfides are relevant.
caveats: Physical confinement and chemical binding are different contributions; the cited cycling results belong to particular implementations.
